observable_outcome: An Increment has a real Git working copy: an independent clone of a Repository, made by the real git binary at a resolved absolute path, living at <workspace_root>/<execution_id>/source inside a rootless user+mount namespace, branched off the base branch, changed, verified at the Git level and committed -- with every write outside that directory refused by the kernel, and with no remote reached, no push argv constructible by the adapter, and no git config written at any scope. The copy is removed when its Execution ends and swept at Runner start if a crash left it behind. A Requirement captured with a repository_id is durably linked to that Repository, the link is write-once, and the Repository detail view's Requirement Backlog reports a repository-scoped count instead of 'unobserved'. application.ServiceConfig.RepositoryID is gone: Plan writes the canonical target's RepositoryID from the link, the Control-Intent snapshot path resolves it from the lease's Increment when no canonical target is stored, and a domain.ScopeRepository Control Intent naming a registered Repository actually matches a planned Increment -- proven by a test with a negative and a positive control. internal/domain/model.go, control.go and lease.go, internal/runner/workspace.go, confinement.go and supervisor.go, contracts/release-contract/**, ci/components.json, Makefile, go.mod, go.sum and devbox.* are unchanged; make check reaches no network; nothing is pushed to any remote.
acceptance_criteria: A1. Fixed implementation order with mid-task stops. Implement in this order and do not begin a leg before the previous one compiles and its tests pass: (1) internal/domain/repository.go (the link value object), (2) internal/application (ports.go member interface, service.go Capture/Plan/snapshot changes and the ServiceConfig.RepositoryID deletion, repository.go backlog view, readmodels.go row field), (3) internal/store/memory, (4) internal/api plus contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml, (5) internal/store/firestore, (6) internal/web, (7) internal/runner/sourcecontrol.go and its deterministic refusal tests, (8) internal/runner/git.go and the real-git real-namespace integration test, (9) the live clone check, (10) docs, (11) evidence. If legs 1 and 2 are not green before leg 4 begins, stop and escalate rather than carrying a broken seam forward. Report, per leg, the argv actually run and its verdict line.

A2. Domain, one file, one additive type. Add to internal/domain/repository.go only: RequirementRepositoryLink{RequirementID, RepositoryID, AssignedAt, RequestedBy} and ValidateRequirementRepositoryLink. Do NOT extend internal/domain/model.go's generic Validate or Decide type switches and do NOT add a field to Requirement, Increment, Execution, Lease, ControlIntent or Repository. internal/domain/model.go, control.go, lease.go, release.go and id.go must be byte-identical at the end; report git diff --stat for internal/domain to prove it. internal/domain/source_guard_test.go must keep passing unmodified.

A3. The link is write-once and validated. A link may be written at most once per Requirement: writing a second link for the same Requirement with a different RepositoryID is a conflict refusal, and writing the identical link again is an idempotent replay, not a second record. ValidateRequirementRepositoryLink refuses an empty or non-opaque identifier on either side and refuses a zero AssignedAt. Assert all four cases.

A4. Capture writes the link with Capture's own ceremony. Add the optional field RepositoryID to CaptureRequest and write the link inside Capture's existing transaction, following Service.Capture step for step: callerActor role check, requestedBy attribution, requireRequest on RequestID, requestFingerprint for idempotency, s.mutate keyed by operation and request id, the Idempotency read that replays a matching fingerprint and refuses a differing one, a domain.Permit gate on domain.PermitIntake with ControlTarget{InstallationID: s.config.InstallationID, RepositoryID: <the supplied id>}, and one s.record event. A Capture naming a Repository that does not exist, or one whose status is retired, is refused and creates no Requirement. A Capture with no RepositoryID keeps working exactly as today and writes no link.

A5. One member interface on the unit of work. Add exactly one interface to internal/application/ports.go -- RequirementRepositoryLinkRepository with SaveRequirementRepositoryLink(ctx, domain.RequirementRepositoryLink) error, RequirementRepositoryLink(ctx, requirementID string) (domain.RequirementRepositoryLink, bool, error), RequirementRepositoryLinks(ctx, ids []string) (map[string]domain.RequirementRepositoryLink, error) and RequirementIDsForRepository(ctx, repositoryID string, limit int) ([]string, bool, error) where the bool reports truncation -- and include it in UnitOfWork. Change no existing port method signature. The batch and the per-repository read must apply their bound in the storage query, matching RequirementReadRepository's stated contract.

A6. Delete ServiceConfig.RepositoryID. Remove the field from internal/application/service.go (declared at L150-154, field at L152) and remove all three reads: L451 (Heartbeat), L751 (Plan) and L1140 (the ControlIntent snapshot fallback). Before deleting, grep the whole tree for a literal that sets it and report the count; the measured count on the starting tree is zero across all 31 ServiceConfig literals. If any caller sets it, STOP and escalate: the deletion is then wrong. Do not add an environment variable, a flag or any other process-level source for a repository id, and do not edit cmd/control-plane/main.go.

A7. Plan writes a real repository id into the canonical target. At internal/application/service.go's Plan path (the SaveCanonicalTarget call near L751), read the captured Requirement's link inside the same transaction and set ControlTarget.RepositoryID from it. A Requirement with no link yields an empty RepositoryID and that is not an error. Assert that after Plan, u.CanonicalTarget for the new Increment returns a target whose RepositoryID equals the registered Repository's id.

A8. The ControlIntent snapshot path resolves a repository when no canonical target is stored. At the fallback near L1140, resolve the repository from lease.IncrementID -> Increment.RequirementID -> the link, so a lease with no stored canonical target still carries a real RepositoryID into its ControlTargetSnapshot. Keep the existing fill-only-when-empty RunnerID merge exactly as it is.

A9. Heartbeat carries no repository, deliberately and provably. Heartbeat's ControlTarget must contain no RepositoryID, and a test named for that fact must assert that a domain.ScopeRepository Control Intent does NOT match a heartbeat target. State the reason in a comment at the call site: HeartbeatRequest (service.go L370-374) carries no increment and no lease, and a Runner is not repository-bound, so attaching a repository would make a repository-scoped stop apply to unrelated work.

A10. The dead control scope is proven alive. Add a test that registers a Repository, captures a Requirement naming it, plans an Increment, requests a domain.ScopeRepository Control Intent naming that repository id, and asserts (i) the stored canonical target's RepositoryID is non-empty and equal to that id -- the positive control, which is the assertion that fails on the starting tree -- (ii) domain.ControlApplies holds for that scope and target, and (iii) the negative control: the same intent with a different repository id does not match and does not appear in the ControlProgress snapshot. internal/domain/control.go must be unchanged; report git diff --stat to prove it.

A11. The fourth observable becomes measured. RepositoryBacklogView gains a repository-scoped Requirement count and a truncation flag, its State becomes ObservedMeasured when the count was actually read, and InstallationScope keeps reporting the Installation-wide summary under its existing name. Update internal/application/repository_test.go TestRepositoryDetailRendersAllSixDeclaredObservables in place -- keep the test name, change the backlog assertion from ObservedUnobserved to the measured count, and keep every other observable's assertion exactly as it is. Do not delete the test and do not add a second one that shadows it.

A12. Rows carry their repository. RequirementView and RequirementDetailView each gain repository_id with omitempty, populated from the batch link read for the ids on the page. An unlinked Requirement omits the field entirely; it never reports a guessed or defaulted repository. captureBody in internal/api/api.go gains repository_id and passes it through. Assert the JSON of both a linked and an unlinked row.

A13. No new Firestore index. The per-repository read is a single-field equality query on the link record's repository id, bounded by Limit(n+1) in the same shape internal/store/firestore/store.go already uses at L850 and L896. firestore.indexes.json must be byte-identical at the end; report git diff --stat to prove it. Both store implementations must satisfy the same tests.

A14. The port, in internal/runner, not in a new package. Add internal/runner/sourcecontrol.go declaring the SourceControl interface with exactly these methods -- Version, Materialize, ApplyChange, VerifyIntegrity, Commit, Discard, RunProjectVerification -- plus WorkingCopy, MaterializeRequest, ChangeSet, ChangeFile, IntegrityObservation, CommitObservation, ProjectVerification and the sentinel errors. Add internal/runner/git.go with the single production implementation GitSourceControl. Create no new Go package and add no third-party dependency: go.mod and go.sum are prohibited paths. Any fake implementation of the port must live in a _test.go file; a non-test file must contain none.

A15. Absolute path and basename, before any process exists. GitSourceControl resolves its executable with the same resolveTool fallback confinement.go and forge.go use, refuses a non-absolute path, refuses a resolved path whose filepath.Base is not "git", and refuses a path that does not stat to a regular file -- all before any child is started, with an injectable Stat hook so the refusals are deterministic and touch no filesystem. Mirror internal/runner/forge.go L122-144 and L296-299. Record the measured baseline: git version 2.55.0, resolved under the devbox nix profile; gh is absent from the devbox run --pure PATH while git and unshare are present, so a bare exec by name is not acceptable.

A16. Closed subcommand allowlist, with push absent by construction. Every argv the adapter can build must name a subcommand from a closed allowlist: version, init, clone, checkout, switch, add, commit, rev-parse, status, diff, fsck, ls-files, cat-file, symbolic-ref. push, fetch, remote, submodule, config, credential and worktree must be absent, and an argv naming one must be refused before a process starts. Assert the refusal for each of push, fetch, remote, config and worktree as positive controls, and assert that the allowlist itself is what refuses them rather than a caller-side check.

A17. Guarded child environment with no HOME. The git child receives exactly PATH, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null, GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null and GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, plus GIT_AUTHOR_DATE and GIT_COMMITTER_DATE on the commit call only, built through buildEnvironmentFromBaseNames-equivalent construction and passed through GuardEnvironment and GuardCommand. HOME must NOT be allowlisted: it was measured that clone, checkout -b, add and commit all succeed without it under git 2.55.0. Committer identity is passed as -c user.name and -c user.email in argv, and the dates come from the injected clock. Assert that a non-allowlisted name is refused and that the environment contains no HOME entry. Do not run git config at repository, global or system scope and do not run gh auth setup-git.

A18. Every writing git child is confined, fail-closed. Each write-capable git command runs through ProcessSupervisor with Confine set to NamespaceConfinement{Workspace: <workspace_root>/<execution_id>}; a Probe failure is returned as a hard error and no child is started unconfined, ever. Every non-clone command carries -C <absolute working copy root> because ProcessSupervisor has no Dir field and internal/runner/supervisor.go is a prohibited path; assert that the built argv contains -C with the absolute root. Only git --version may run unconfined, and only because it writes nothing; say so in a comment.

A19. Real git, real kernel, real refusals (docs/architecture/validation.md L84). One integration test, inside make check, must: create a bare origin at test time with the real git binary in t.TempDir(); clone it with --no-hardlinks into <workspace_root>/<execution_id>/source inside the namespace; assert git rev-parse --git-common-dir returns ".git", proving an independent repository rather than a linked worktree; create the branch; apply a ChangeSet; run the Git-level verification; commit; and assert that a write to the sealed ancestor and a write to the origin directory both fail, and that a write into a sibling Execution's directory fails. Nothing may be faked: no fake git, no fake namespace, no fake signal. Log the resolved absolute git path, git --version, uname -srm and the top-level ancestor the confinement sealed.

A20. The positive control validation.md L84 demands by name. In the same test file, perform the identical outside-workspace write WITHOUT applying the namespace and assert that it SUCCEEDS. Without this control the EROFS result proves nothing about the namespace. Report both verdicts side by side in the runner evidence.

A21. Git-level verification is executed, project-level verification is declared and fails closed. VerifyIntegrity must actually run status --porcelain=v2, diff --exit-code HEAD, rev-parse for HEAD and the base, fsck --no-progress --connectivity-only and cat-file on the committed tree, and return a bounded IntegrityObservation carrying the head commit name, the tree name, the base commit name, the branch, the clean flag and the changed-path count. RunProjectVerification must return ErrProjectVerificationNotWired, start no process, and be proven by an AST control in a test that its body constructs no exec call. Never report the project-level stage as passed.

A22. No process output ever leaves the adapter. stdout is captured into a bounded buffer with a hard byte cap, stderr is discarded, and no error returned by the adapter carries child output, a path outside the workspace, or any credential-shaped value. Parse failures return a sentinel whose message contains none of the input, mirroring internal/runner/forge.go L58-64 and L296-315.

A23. Working copy location and lifetime. The copy is at <workspace_root>/<execution_id>/source, produced by the existing Workspace.Create(execution_id) followed by the clone into the source child; internal/runner/workspace.go must be byte-identical at the end. Write a plain-text descriptor beside it naming increment_id, execution_id, repository_id and created_at, with no credential-shaped field. Discard must be idempotent, must refuse any root that fails the same escape check Workspace.Path applies, and must be called on the error path too. Assert that a working copy is never shared between two Executions: a second Execution of the same Increment gets a fresh clone at its own path.

A24. Crash cleanup is swept, deterministically. Add SweepWorkingCopies(active) which removes every workspace child whose execution id is not in the active set, and prove it without a goroutine, a sleep or a timer: create two working copies, mark one active, construct a fresh provider over the same workspace root, sweep, and assert the inactive tree is gone, the active one is intact, and the origin repository is byte-identical before and after (compare a recursive digest or git -C <origin> rev-parse --all). Assert also that Sweep refuses to remove anything outside the workspace root.

A25. Two clone-source regimes, no network in make check. Inside make check the origin is always a bare repository created at test time by the real git binary in t.TempDir(); no git fixture, pack file or bare directory may be committed to this repository, and no test inside make check may resolve a hostname or open a socket. The single live check is gated on AGENTIC_LOOP_LIVE_GIT=1 together with AGENTIC_LOOP_LIVE_GIT_CLONE_URL supplied by the owner; it clones anonymously with --depth 1 --no-tags and GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, asserts the resulting HEAD resolves, and creates nothing on the remote. If AGENTIC_LOOP_LIVE_GIT=1 is set and the URL is absent the test FAILS with a message naming the missing designation; it does not skip. When the gate is unset it skips and the skip is recorded with status "skipped" and its reason, never as a pass.

A26. Leave no refs behind (docs/architecture/validation.md L187). Every commit this task's tests create must live in a temporary repository outside this repository's working tree; no branch, tag or ref may be created in this repository other than the task branch itself. Before finishing, run git for-each-ref in the task worktree and report that it names no probe or working-copy ref.

A27. Owner console, appended block only. If internal/web/owner.js or internal/web/owner.html is edited, append a self-contained block at the end of the file introduced by a marker comment naming V2-071; do not rewrite or reformat the existing single-line content. The block must render the Repository detail's repository-scoped Requirement Backlog count and the Requirement Backlog's per-row repository, and must show an absent measurement as its explicit state and reason rather than as a plausible value.

A28. OpenAPI is the contract of record. Declare every changed request and response field in contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml: repository_id on the capture request body, repository_id on the requirement list and detail responses, and the repository-scoped backlog shape on the repository detail response. contracts/schemas/** and contracts/release-contract/** must be byte-identical; report git diff --stat for contracts/ to prove it.

A29. Evidence, nine records, keys read from the final green tree. Write one evidence record per touched component -- domain, application, store-memory, store-firestore, api, web, contracts, runner, docs -- register each in .agents/v2/evidence/index.json with task_id V2-071 as the producer, and make the ledger tests in internal/contracts green as the definition of done. Read each component evidence key from make evidence-keys on the final green tree, after removing build/evidence and after committing the evidence, then confirm make check is green on that commit. Record in every record: machine and kernel from uname -srm, go version, devbox environment, and the resolved absolute git path with its version. Note, without repairing it, that control-plane's evidence key can move through its declared contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml dependency while its roots are unchanged.

A30. Counts, verdicts and skips. Report the before and after top-level test count per touched package. The measured baseline on the starting tree is: internal/domain 37, internal/application 49, internal/store/memory 4, internal/store/firestore 9, internal/api 20, internal/runner 67, internal/contracts 30, internal/ci 11. Every pre-existing test must keep passing under its existing name with its assertions unchanged, except the one deliberate change A11 authorises. Judge every devbox run by its verdict line, not by devbox run's exit code. A skipped test is never counted as a pass.
constraints: Work only inside the assigned isolated task worktree; never push.
Never use git reset, git checkout --, git stash or git commit --amend.

Do not touch ci/components.json, ci/**, Makefile, go.mod, go.sum or devbox.*. V2-045's manifest surface check (internal/ci TestManifestDependencySurface, TestDerivedGraphMatchesDeclaredNarrowings) will turn make check red if a new import edge is undeclared: if that happens, STOP and escalate to the tech_lead. Do not edit the manifest to make it pass.
Do not touch .agents/v2/task-state/** or any .agents/v2/packets/** file; the coordinator records transitions and packets.

internal/domain/control.go, internal/domain/model.go and internal/domain/lease.go are untouchable. The Requirement-to-Repository link is a new value object in internal/domain/repository.go with its own validate function, following the control.go/lease.go/release.go precedent and the ControlRequestedByRepository side-table precedent.

internal/runner/workspace.go, confinement.go, supervisor.go, secret_guard.go, secret_broker.go, forge.go and source_guard_test.go are untouchable. The Git adapter reuses them as they are: Workspace.Create for the path, NamespaceConfinement plus ProcessSupervisor for the confinement, GuardEnvironment and GuardCommand for the environment, and -C in argv because ProcessSupervisor has no Dir field.
Do not touch contracts/release-contract/** or contracts/schemas/**. No capability declaration may be weakened, narrowed or reinterpreted to match the result. Do not claim cap-autonomous-resolution.

No remote write of any kind. No push, no fetch that writes, no branch, ref, tag, release or PR on any remote. The adapter's argv allowlist must not contain push, fetch, remote, submodule, config, credential or worktree, and the kernel refusal measured inside the namespace must remain the second independent guarantee.

Do not run git config at repository, global or system scope, and do not run gh auth setup-git. Configuration is pinned per invocation with GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null, GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null and -c options in argv.
Do not allowlist HOME into the git child's environment. It was measured unnecessary, and excluding it is what proves by absence that the adapter cannot reach the user's credential store.

Do not start a real Provider CLI (codex/claude/opencode), do not start gh, and do not touch any Google Cloud resource. The only external process this task may start is git, and the only network use is the single AGENTIC_LOOP_LIVE_GIT-gated anonymous clone.
make check must reach no network. No test inside make check may resolve a hostname, open a socket or clone from a remote.

Never fake git, the namespace or a signal in the gate-bearing integration test (docs/architecture/validation.md L84). If the kernel refuses unprivileged user namespaces, STOP and escalate with the recorded kernel identifier and Probe's reason; do not skip and count it as a pass.

Determinism is acceptance, not preference: no fixed sleep, no wall-clock timer and no goroutine in any new test. Waiting is expressed only as bounded deadline polling with an injected clock, and a measured duration is logged as an observation, never asserted as a threshold.

A skipped test is never counted as a pass (gate rule G7). Record every skip explicitly with status "skipped" and its reason. A local, emulated or faked result may never be registered as satisfying a condition that names a real remote (G3.1).
Record the execution environment identifier in every evidence record: machine and kernel from uname -srm, go version, devbox environment, and the resolved absolute git path with its version.
No credential value, prompt or raw child response is retained in any source file, record, document, log or evidence summary, in any form. stderr is discarded and stdout is bounded.
Commit no git fixture and leave no probe ref: gitleaks git scans every ref, so a commit created by a test must live only in a temporary repository outside this working tree.

When writing a digest into prose, match the .gitleaks.toml allowlist form: a bare 64-hex or 40-hex value followed by at most one punctuation character. Prefer naming the kind of digest over quoting its value.

Never write a verification as passed that was not actually executed. If an acceptance item cannot be satisfied, STOP and escalate to the tech_lead rather than fabricating, weakening or reinterpreting it.

Escalate rather than proceed if: any ServiceConfig literal in the tree sets RepositoryID; make check goes red on the manifest surface check; the ScopeRepository matching proof would need a change to internal/domain/control.go; the namespace Probe fails in this environment; the resolved git version is older than 2.32 (GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL support); or a top-level test count decreases in any touched package.

Rollback is source-only: this task creates no external effect and writes no remote, so reverting the commits on the task branch and deleting the branch restores the prior state completely. The link records are additive and empty for every pre-existing Requirement, and deleting ServiceConfig.RepositoryID removes a field no stored record references.
Judge every devbox run by its verdict line ("E2E group passed", "Lint passed", make check's own final verdict), not by the exit code of devbox run, which is unreliable in this environment.
